walkthroughs.body_html:
Breathing & Respiration — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Breathing & Respiration brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Breathing & Respiration.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Aerobic respiration releases energy from glucose using:
options: nitrogen
oxygen
carbon dioxide
water
endothermic
exothermic
always anaerobic
only in plants
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
Respiration means breathing — inhaling oxygen and exhaling carbon dioxide.
A series of chemical reactions in cells that break down glucose to release energy as ATP.
Respiration is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
Yes — plants respire all the time to release energy; they also photosynthesise when there is light.
Plants only photosynthesise and do not respire; respiration is for animals only.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.

mcqs.q: What is produced in anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
options: Respiration is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight.
Anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and CO2 in humans.
Lactic acid (lactate) and a small amount of ATP — no CO2 or water in this pathway.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.

options: 21 moles
18 moles
17 moles
13 moles

mcqs.q: A student breathes out onto a cold mirror and it mists up; breathing into limewater turns it cloudy. Which two substances are shown to be in exhaled air?
options: Water vapour and carbon dioxide
Oxygen and nitrogen
Glucose and oxygen
Lactic acid and ethanol

mcqs.q: After exercise a person continues to breathe heavily for several minutes. Which best explains this?
options: Extra oxygen is needed to break down lactic acid built up.
The lungs need to cool down after exercise.
The body is storing oxygen for later.
Anaerobic respiration has stopped all breathing.

mcqs.q: Which word equation correctly represents aerobic respiration?
options: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water (+ energy)
carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen
glucose → lactic acid (+ energy)
glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide

mcqs.q: Why does aerobic respiration release more energy per glucose molecule than anaerobic respiration?
options: Glucose is more completely broken down when oxygen is used.
Anaerobic respiration uses more oxygen.
Aerobic respiration does not produce any waste.
Anaerobic respiration breaks glucose down completely.
